sections.h2: Where is Montgomery County, Alabama, and how large is it?
sections.html:
Montgomery County sits in the central part of Alabama and holds the state capital, Montgomery, as its county seat and largest municipality. The Census Bureau lists 800 square miles in total, of which 784 are land and 16 are water.

The legislature carved the county out of Monroe County on December 6, 1816. It carries the name of Lemuel P. Montgomery, a young Army officer killed at the Battle of Horseshoe Bend. Seven counties touch it: Elmore, Macon, Bullock, Pike, Crenshaw, Lowndes and Autauga.

ItemMontgomery County
EstablishedDecember 6, 1816
County seatMontgomery
Total area800 square miles (784 land)
2020 census population228,954, seventh in the state
2025 estimate225,891
Housing units, 2020105,293, with 11.5% vacant
Owner-occupied share, 202056.3% of occupied homes

Those figures come from Wikipedia's county article, which cites the Census Bureau. The county count slipped slightly between 2010 and 2020, from 229,363 to 228,954, and the 2025 estimate is lower again.

sections.h2: What shaped the Montgomery County economy?
sections.html:
Cotton built the county's wealth through most of the 1800s, and government, rail, river shipping and military aviation carry it now. The boll weevil arrived in 1914 and hit the cotton harvest hard from 1915 on, and by the 1940s county farms earned more from cattle than from cotton.

Today the county's footing is institutional. The capital brings state offices, and the county has shipping hubs on the Alabama River and rail hubs in the city of Montgomery. Maxwell Air Force Base houses the Air War College, and the county lists several colleges and universities, among them Alabama State University, Auburn University Montgomery, Huntingdon College, Faulkner University and Troy University at Montgomery.

The county is also a renter-heavy place. About 43.7% of occupied homes in the county were renter-occupied in 2020, so inherited rentals and tired landlord properties are a regular part of the local resale picture.

sections.h2: Which roads, airport and transit serve Montgomery County?
sections.html:
Interstate 65 and Interstate 85 cross in the county. U.S. 80, U.S. 82, U.S. 231, U.S. 31 and U.S. 331 add surface routes, and the county article lists a long run of state routes as well.

  • Montgomery Regional Airport handles passenger service plus military and commercial aviation.
  • The Montgomery Area Transit System provides local transit.
  • The Selma to Montgomery National Historic Trail passes through part of the county.

Pintlala, Snowdoun and Mount Meigs are unincorporated communities in the county, so houses there sit outside city limits and a buyer should confirm which services and taxes apply.

sections.h2: Which school districts and communities are in Montgomery County?
sections.html:
Montgomery Public Schools serves most of the county, with its headquarters at 307 S. Decatur Street. Pike Road City School District runs the public schools in Pike Road, and the on-base school at Maxwell Air Force Base is operated by the Department of Defense Education Activity.

The county has one city, Montgomery, and two towns, Hope Hull and Pike Road. Unincorporated places include Ada, Cecil, Grady, Le Grand, Mathews, Pintlala, Ramer and Waugh. Which taxing area a house sits in matters, because a city address and a rural address can receive different bills even when the street looks the same on a map.

sections.h2: When are Montgomery County property taxes due, and what happens if they go unpaid?
sections.html:
Alabama property taxes are due October 1 and become delinquent after December 31. The Alabama Department of Revenue lays out the usual sequence for unpaid bills.

MonthStep
October 1Taxes due
January 1Taxes delinquent
FebruaryTurned over to probate court
MarchProbate court meets
AprilAdvertised for sale
MayTax sale

In Montgomery County the lien date is October 1 of the year before the tax year. The county's appraisal appeals page gives October 1, 2023 as the lien date for tax year 2024, which shows that the bill you pay in the fall reflects ownership and condition a year earlier.

sections.h2: How do you appeal a Montgomery County assessment?
sections.html:
You appeal to the county Board of Equalization, and the county says the deadline is thirty days from the date printed on your notice. The Board of Equalization appeals page states that there is no filing fee.

  • File by email at propertytaxappeals@mc-ala.org, or call (334) 832-1327 for real property and (334) 832-1375 for personal property.
  • No special form is required, but the Board wants an original signature.
  • Send the supporting papers with the appeal. The county names closing statements, appraisals, comparable sales and insurance values as examples.
  • An informal review before the deadline is available and the county recommends it.
  • Out-of-state agents may file, and an attorney is not required, but the agent must supply a signed authorization.

The county's own FAQ was written for tax year 2024, and it says comparable sales for that year came from October 1, 2022 through September 30, 2023. Check the current notice for the dates that apply to your year.

Official source: Montgomery County appraisal appeals FAQ.

sections.h2: What homestead exemptions can lower a Montgomery County tax bill?
sections.html:
The state homestead exemption applies to a single-family home that you own and live in as your primary residence on the first day of the tax year, on up to 160 acres. The Alabama Department of Revenue says you apply at your local county office.

Owner typeState exemption
Under 65, not disabledUp to $4,000 of assessed value
Age 65 or olderNo maximum on the state portion
Permanently and totally disabledNo maximum on the state portion
BlindNo maximum on the state portion

County exemptions are separate and carry their own income tests, so a retiree should ask the county office which type applies. Selling the house ends the exemption for the next owner, who must apply on their own.

sections.h2: What does selling a Montgomery County house involve at the courthouse?
sections.html:
A deed is recorded with the judge of probate, and state law attaches a recordation tax of 50 cents for each $500 of value conveyed. A $160,000 sale price, for example, would produce a tax of $160 under that formula. The statute lets the amount be reduced by a mortgage on which the mortgage tax was already paid.

The recording office asks for proof of the real price paid. The law adds a penalty of $100 or 25% of the tax due, whichever is greater, if someone intentionally withholds that proof after a request. A title or escrow company normally handles the paperwork, but you should know the rule exists.

If a tax bill is open at closing, ask the title company how it will be paid from proceeds. For a deceased owner's house, the personal representative has to be in place before anyone can sign a deed.

sections.h2: What do Montgomery County sellers usually face, and when does a cash sale fit?
sections.html:
Sellers here often deal with inherited property, rental houses with tenants, deferred repairs and unpaid tax bills. A cash purchase that closes as-is can suit those cases because it avoids repair bids, showings and a buyer's loan approval.

  • Inherited homes: heirs may live elsewhere and not want a long probate listing.
  • Rentals: owners may prefer to sell without clearing the unit first.
  • Back taxes: a fast sale can pay the amount due out of proceeds.
  • Older houses: no repair list is required before an as-is closing.

Cash Home Buyers reviews Montgomery County houses in their present condition and gives a written offer. You decide whether the number works for your situation, and you owe nothing if you say no.

faqs.q: How much is the Montgomery County property tax appeal fee?
faqs.a: There is no fee. The county's Board of Equalization FAQ says filing an appeal costs nothing, though you must file within thirty days of the date on your notice.

faqs.q: When are property taxes due in Montgomery County, Alabama?
faqs.a: They are due October 1 and delinquent after December 31, per the Alabama Department of Revenue. Unpaid accounts move toward a probate court process that ends in a tax sale in May.

faqs.q: Who runs the county assessment appeals in Montgomery County?
faqs.a: The Board of Equalization, working with the county Appraisal Department. Real property appeals go to propertytaxappeals@mc-ala.org or (334) 832-1327.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Montgomery County house with back taxes owed?
faqs.a: Yes. Ask the county for the amount owed and the title company how it will be paid at closing. A cash buyer can often fold that payoff into the sale.
